name: FoundationDB
tagline: Apple's ordered, strictly serializable distributed key-value store, built to have layers on top.
description: FoundationDB is a distributed, ordered key-value store that gives you multi-key ACID transactions with strict serializability across a whole cluster, and almost nothing else on purpose. Higher-level data models (records, documents, SQL, queues) are built as stateless 'layers' on top, which is how Apple runs CloudKit and Snowflake runs its metadata catalog on it. Its deterministic simulation testing is legendary and it is among the most correctness-focused databases you can run. The trade-offs are hard limits (5-second transactions, 10 MB transaction size, 100 KB values) and the need to build or adopt a layer for anything beyond raw keys.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; no official managed service.

scale.notes: Automatic range sharding and rebalancing; multi-region configurations replicate synchronously to a satellite and fail over to a standby region.

strengths: Strictly serializable multi-key transactions across the whole cluster
Deterministic simulation testing gives exceptional reliability
Ordered keyspace enables efficient range scans and custom indexes
Layer architecture: Record Layer and others add data models on a common core
Self-healing: automatic data distribution, replication and recovery
weaknesses: Transactions limited to 5 seconds and 10 MB; values capped at 100 KB
Raw key-value API: you must build or adopt a layer for documents, SQL or secondary indexes
No official managed service and a steep operational learning curve
Smaller community; much development happens inside Apple and Snowflake
useCases: Metadata stores for larger systems (catalogs, object stores)
Foundation for custom databases and layers
Multi-tenant app backends via the Record Layer
notIdealFor: Teams wanting SQL out of the box
